text:
alex: Heads-up — new RFP from a regulated financial customer. They want to run Redwood fully air-gapped. Key asks: operator-based installs OR an immutable offline bundle, clear upgrade cadence, signed artifacts, and pricing for offline support.

maria: Got it. Summarizing asks so we have a checklist: 1) packaging options (operator vs immutable bundle) 2) upgrade/patch cadence options 3) artifact signing & SBOM process 4) activation key model and token policy 5) pricing add-on for offline support/POC.

sam: We support both paths. Operator: requires k8s cluster access during install and can handle rolling updates via controller images. Immutable bundle: single tarball with images, manifests, SBOM, signatures, and an activation key for install — intended for no-egress sites.

joanne: Legal/Compliance note: every offline bundle must include an SBOM and signed provenance. We also need a cert-rotation doc and guidance for integrating with customer KMS/HSM (if they want key custody).

ryan: From infra ops: delta patches are supported but only through signed patch bundles that the customer applies. We don’t permit unsigned diffs. Typical offering: monthly security-only patches + quarterly feature bundles. For highly conservative customers we can lock to quarterly-only deliveries.

alex: For a cautious bank, recommend defaults?

sam: Recommend monthly security patches and quarterly full upgrades as the baseline. Offer a locked quarterly cadence as an opt-in.

maria: How do activation keys work? Per-bundle one-time keys or site tokens?

ops-bot: deploybot: offline-activation: supports both per-bundle short-lived keys and long-lived site tokens. Security default: per-bundle short-lived keys. Long-lived tokens only for low-risk profiles and with additional contractual safeguards.

joanne: Commercially: propose two fee lines — base on-prem license + platform fee, and an "offline-support" SOW that covers bundle signing, SBOM generation, validation testing, and delivery windows. For air-gapped POCs we typically charge a fixed packaging & validation fee (unless there's a strategic concession).

ryan: Important technical detail — if the site has zero egress, we include all verification keys and CRLs in the bundle. If limited egress is allowed, we can offer an offline-checkin stub to validate revocation. We should document both flows.

alex: Can we paste the offline install example we hand to customers?

sam: Example bootstrap we share with ops teams:

```
# bootstrap offline bundle
redwoodctl install --bundle /tmp/redwood-offline-2026-01.tgz \\
  --activation-key xxxxx-REDACTED-xxxxx \\
  --sbom /tmp/sbom.json \\
  --verify-signature /tmp/signature.sig
```

sam: For operator installs we include a controller image within the bundle and pinned CRD manifests (image digests). Upgrades occur by applying a new signed bundle which updates CRD image digests — operator reconciles the rollout.

maria: Action items: sam to draft a short "packaging options" one-pager + sample offline SOW; joanne to draft pricing lines and contract language about token policy; ryan to put together a test matrix for no-egress and limited-egress installs (including smoke tests and rollback steps). Aim to respond to the customer by EOD tomorrow.

alex: If there are blockers (signing infra, legal redlines, or support SLA concerns) call them out here. Otherwise let's align and send the proposal. :thumbsup:
